dimensions.note: Re-reviewed for `subject`. The new field is an IDENTIFIER, never credential material, and parsePveSubject REJECTS any subject containing '=' precisely so a pasted `tokenid=<secret>` cannot be written into a resource attribute or a detail string — a test asserts that rejection. The subject is echoed in `detail` deliberately, which is safe because it names a token rather than proving anything about it. The authenticating secret still travels only as an Authorization header and is still absent from every returned detail.

This revision adds no logging. All logging remains in the audit method — one structured line per credential plus a completion line — and the new probe returns a ProbeResult rather than emitting anything itself, so it cannot introduce a secret onto a log path.

Unchanged in shape, extended in coverage. A malformed `subject` returns authFailed and — importantly — does NOT fall back to reporting the authenticating token, which would silently report the wrong credential as healthy. A subject absent from its user's token map is authFailed, not noExpiry. Both have tests. probePveToken still cannot throw.

45 tests, 5 new for `subject`. The central one is a regression test for the defect this revision fixes: authenticating as a monitor whose own token never expires while reporting on a provisioning token that does — asserting both the URL targets the SUBJECT's user and that the reported expiry is the subject's. Also covered: identifier-vs-secret rejection, no-subject self-report unchanged, malformed subject not falling back, and subject missing from the map.

Read-only by construction: the new probe is a single GET, and the model still exposes no method that can create, rotate or revoke anything. Verified empirically against a live cluster rather than by reading the code — the monitoring token this probe is built for returns 403 to both `POST /access/users/{u}/token/{new}` and `POST /nodes/{n}/qemu/{id}/status/stop`. Re-running is inherently safe; a partially completed run leaves no external state.

Unchanged endpoint. `subject` only changes WHICH userid is requested, and the response is read with the same typeof guards. Verified against a live cluster that a PVEAuditor token reads /access/users/{other-user} for every user in the realm, which is what makes one probe credential sufficient for a whole cluster.

No file handles, sockets or temp files. One fetch, with AbortSignal.timeout(globalArgs.timeoutMs) as on every other probe. The response body is consumed exactly once, inside a try, on the only path that reads it. The model creates no external resources, so there is nothing to track for cleanup.

Re-checked. The README example uses `builder@pve!provisioner` and a `store` vault; the new tests use `terraform@pve!tf-proxmox-docker`, which is a Proxmox realm identifier rather than a hostname, and carries no domain, address or account. Grep for the internal domain, RFC1918 literals and the tailnet suffix across extensions/ and README.md returns nothing.

`subject` is z.string().default("") — always present after parse, never undefined, so downstream code has no optional-vs-empty ambiguity. It is declared on the shared CredentialInputSchema and documented as pve-token-only rather than being silently ignored elsewhere; a non-pve kind that sets it is simply not read, which is visible in the schema description.
Unchanged. Both resources remain lifetime 'infinite' with garbageCollection 30. This revision adds no resource spec, so nothing accumulates that was not already bounded.

Not applicable by design, and deliberately so: the model has a single `audit` method and no create/update/delete surface. That absence is the safety argument for scheduling it unattended against production credentials, and this revision preserves it — the new kind adds a read, not a write.

preflight() is unchanged and still refuses the whole run on duplicate ids or ids that collide after normalisation. The new probe adds a per-credential fail-fast of its own: a secret not in `user@realm!tokenid=<secret>` form returns before any network call, which a test asserts by flagging the stub rather than by inspecting only the status.

resourceNameFor is unchanged and normalises a pve-token id such as `pve-token/terraform@pve!tf-proxmox-docker` to `pve-token-terraform-pve-tf-proxmox-docker`. The `@` and `!` characters common in Proxmox ids all fall into the same replacement class, which makes post-normalisation collisions MORE likely for this kind than for the others — two ids differing only in those characters would map to one instance and silently overwrite. That is precisely the case preflight() already refuses the run over, so the risk is detected rather than latent, and it is covered by an existing test.

The model reads no data artifacts — it writes resources and returns a summary. `data.latest()` appears only in the consuming workflow, not in this code, so nothing here can be broken by an instance-name change or a missing prior instance.

Adds a second upgrades entry terminating at 2026.09.08.2. The push check enforces that the chain END at the current version, not merely contain it — I had them newest-first and it was rejected, so the order is now oldest-first. Migration is a no-op: `subject` defaults to empty and an empty subject preserves the previous self-reporting behaviour exactly.
